## Administration

Chief Administrative Officer

The village operates on what is called the “one employee” system. The Chief Administrative Officer (CAO) is council’s only employee and acts as the link between council and the rest of the village staff. The CAO position is responsible for the overall management of village operations; ensuring policies, programs and other directions of council are implemented and advising council on the operation and affairs of the village.

The CAO directs and manages the daily administration of the Village and, in this capacity, ensures the delivery of high quality services in a timely, responsible and cost-effective manner. In addition, the CAO is responsible for the personnel function of the Village and maintains staff communication. She is also responsible for the oversight of contracted services. Acting as Approving Officer, the CAO oversees all subdivision development and related planning matters.

The CAO is a statutory position under the Community Charter and the incumbent is appointed by Council.

## Finance

Chief Financial Officer

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is responsible for the financial services for the Village. They oversee the investment of municipal funds, the expenditure of the Village’s money and ensure that accurate records and full accounts of the Village’s financial affairs are prepared and maintained. They develop short and long range financial forecasts and plans, supervise financial employees and oversees the financial information systems.

The CFO works with the Council and the CAO on the annual budget process and development of the Five-Year Financial Plan. Part of this process is the presentation to Council of varying options regarding property tax rates and user fees for the upcoming year.

The Village also maintains financial transparency through annual audits. Every year, external auditors examine the financial system and annual statements, and report their findings to Council.

# Financial Plans and Reports

## 5 Year Financial Plans

The Community Charter requires that all municipalities adopt a Five-Year Financial Plan each year prior to the adoption of the annual property tax bylaw. The purpose of the Five-Year Financial Plan is to provide a budgetary framework for the District to plan the management of its resources, revenues and expenditures in order to best serve the community. The current year in the five-year financial plan forms the annual budget, while following years provides a guideline, incorporating various long-term plans and strategies.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Reporting directly to the Chief Administrative Officer, this is a broad senior leadership role with significant responsibility for the Village's financial direction and operations. You will provide strategic and operational leadership across the Village's financial services functions while contributing to corporate governance and organizational priorities.

As CFO, you will lead the Village's Five-Year Financial Plan, annual operating and capital budgets, financial reporting, forecasting, year-end financial statements and external audit, while ensuring appropriate financial controls, policies and statutory requirements are maintained.

You will oversee core municipal financial operations, including accounts payable and receivable, payroll, taxation, utility billing, investments and reserves, and provide financial leadership for asset management, infrastructure planning, borrowing, grants and funding strategies.
